verifiedSources.title: General
verifiedSources.fullText:
1 GENERAL

1.1 Definitions
The following definitions apply to parts A and B of this Code.
1.1.1 "International Safety Management (ISM) Code" means the International Management Code for the Safe Operation of Ships and for Pollution Prevention as adopted by the Assembly, as may be amended by the Organization.
1.1.2 "Company" means the Owner of the ship or any other organization or person such as the Manager, or the Bareboat Charterer, who has assumed the responsibility for operation of the ship from the Shipowner and who on assuming such responsibility has agreed to take over all the duties and responsibility imposed by the Code.
1.1.3 "Administration" means the Government of the State whose flag the ship is entitled to fly.

1.2 Objectives
1.2.1 The objectives of the Code are to ensure safety at sea, prevention of human injury or loss of life, and avoidance of damage to the environment, in particular to the marine environment and to property.
1.2.2 Safety management objectives of the Company should, inter alia:
.1 provide for safe practices in ship operation and a safe working environment;
.2 assess all identified risks to its ships, personnel and the environment and establish appropriate safeguards; and
.3 continuously improve safety management skills of personnel ashore and aboard ships, including preparing for emergencies related both to safety and environmental protection.
1.2.3 The safety management system should ensure:
.1 compliance with mandatory rules and regulations; and
.2 that applicable codes, guidelines and standards recommended by the Organization, Administrations, classification societies and maritime industry organizations are taken into account.

1.3 Application
The requirements of this Code may be applied to all ships.

1.4 Functional requirements for a safety-management system (SMS)
Every Company should develop, implement and maintain a safety-management system (SMS) which includes the following functional requirements:
.1 a safety and environmental-protection policy;
.2 instructions and procedures to ensure safe operation of ships and protection of the environment in compliance with relevant international and flag State legislation;
.3 defined levels of authority and lines of communication between, and amongst, shore and shipboard personnel;
.4 procedures for reporting accidents and non-conformities with the provisions of this Code;
.5 procedures to prepare for and respond to emergency situations; and
.6 procedures for internal audits and management reviews.
verifiedSources.scopeNote: 1.1 lists only definitions 1.1.1-1.1.3 (Grok's stated scope). Gemini's independent output additionally supplied 1.1.4 through 1.1.12 as a superset, not a contradiction. Claude Code independently confirmed via a live web search today that 1.1.4 (Safety Management System), 1.1.5 (Document of Compliance) and 1.1.6 (Safety Management Certificate) do genuinely exist in the current ISM Code - consistent with Gemini's superset - but did not independently verify the exact wording of 1.1.4-1.1.12 word for word in this pass, only that they exist and roughly match. Treat the extended definitions as plausible, not yet fully character-verified.
verifiedSources.variantNote: Gemini's fullText renders the 1.4 heading and opening sentence as 'Functional requirements for a safety management system' / 'a safety management system' - no hyphen, no '(SMS)' abbreviation - versus Grok's 'safety-management system (SMS)'. Claude Code independently fetched a mirror of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) today: it renders the heading as 'Functional requirements for a Safety Management System (SMS)' - capitalized, and crucially DOES include the '(SMS)' abbreviation, which Gemini's version omits entirely. This does not fully match either AI's exact styling (case and hyphen placement both differ from both), but on the substantive question of whether '(SMS)' appears at all, it supports Grok's version over Gemini's. Note this fetch was extracted via an AI summarization step, not a raw byte-level diff, so treat the exact punctuation as indicative, not a legal-grade citation.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)). Para 1.2.2.2 was amended by resolution MSC.273(85) (adopted 4 December 2008, in force 1 July 2010) to its current risk-assessment wording - NOT by MSC.104(73) as one earlier Gemini note claimed. MSC.104(73) (adopted 5 December 2000, in force 1 July 2002) instead introduced the additional 1.1 definitions (including 1.1.4 onward) and did not touch 1.2.2.2. This correction was independently re-verified by Claude Code today via two searches that did not rely on the four links originally supplied (results included safety4sea.com and an ABS guidance document specifically titled 'Guidance on the Revised ISM Code Clause 1.2.2.2', plus a separate search confirming MSC.104(73)'s 5 Dec 2000 / 1 Jul 2002 dates and its role adding 1.1 definitions).
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok and Gemini independently verbatim-agreed on 1.2, 1.3 and (substantively) 1.4; Claude Code additionally cross-checked the amendment attribution via independent web search (distinct sources from the four originally supplied) and fetched a mirror of the 1993 original text directly.

verifiedSources.title: Safety and Environmental-Protection Policy
verifiedSources.fullText:
2 SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENTAL-PROTECTION POLICY

2.1 The Company should establish a safety and environmental-protection policy which describes how the objectives, given in paragraph 1.2, will be achieved.

2.2 The Company should ensure that the policy is implemented and maintained at all levels of the organization both ship based as well as shore based.
verifiedSources.variantNote: Gemini renders 2.2 as 'both ship-based and shore-based' (hyphenated, 'and'). Claude Code independently fetched a mirror of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) today and it reads 'both ship based as well as shore based' - matching Grok's phrasing exactly, not Gemini's. Treated as Gemini reflecting a later consolidated-edition style rather than the 1993 original, not an error, but the 1993 original itself now directly supports Grok's exact wording here.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)). No amendment identified to paras 2.1-2.2 in any source consulted.
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok gave identical text across two independent rounds (an initial round and a blind re-ask that did not see the first round's answer or any flag of a discrepancy). Claude Code independently verified para 2.1's verb via a live web search today (found 'establish' via an unrelated synthesis, not sourced from the four links originally supplied) and by directly fetching a mirror of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com), which also reads 'establish'.
verifiedSources.knownDiscrepancy: Gemini independently produced 'develop' instead of 'establish' in para 2.1, reproducibly across two rounds (an initial round and a blind re-ask). This contradicts Grok and contradicts both independent checks Claude Code performed today (a web search and a direct fetch of a 1993-original-text mirror, admiraltylawguide.com). Documented here as a reproducible Gemini error on this specific point, not silently dropped or averaged away. Claude Code did not itself independently confirm the previously-claimed ClassNK or University of Washington mirrors specifically - a ClassNK fetch attempt today returned HTTP 403, and the University of Washington PDF was seen only inside a web-search result summary, not fetched directly - so those two sources are not claimed as personally verified here, only the admiraltylawguide.com fetch and the independent web search are.

verifiedSources.title: Company Responsibilities and Authority
verifiedSources.fullText:
3 COMPANY RESPONSIBILITIES AND AUTHORITY

3.1 If the entity who is responsible for the operation of the ship is other than the owner, the owner must report the full name and details of such entity to the Administration.

3.2 The Company should define and document the responsibility, authority and interrelation of all personnel who manage, perform and verify work relating to and affecting safety and pollution prevention.

3.3 The Company is responsible for ensuring that adequate resources and shore-based support are provided to enable the designated person or persons to carry out their functions.
verifiedSources.variantNote: None - Grok and Gemini produced character-for-character identical text.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)). No amendment identified to paras 3.1-3.3 in any source consulted.
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok and Gemini independently verbatim-agreed. Claude Code additionally fetched a mirror of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) directly today and confirmed the same three paragraphs (that mirror renders 3.3 as 'shore based support', without a hyphen, versus the hyphenated 'shore-based' in the Grok/Gemini text above - a minor, non-substantive styling difference, noted rather than silently normalized).

verifiedSources.title: Designated Person(s)
verifiedSources.fullText:
4 DESIGNATED PERSON(S)

To ensure the safe operation of each ship and to provide a link between the company and those on board, every company, as appropriate, should designate a person or persons ashore having direct access to the highest level of management. The responsibility and authority of the designated person or persons should include monitoring the safety and pollution prevention aspects of the operation of each ship and to ensure that adequate resources and shore based support are applied, as required.
verifiedSources.variantNote: Gemini's version paraphrases this into modern consolidated style ('Company' capitalized, 'and ensuring' instead of 'and to ensure', hyphenated 'pollution-prevention'/'shore-based'). Claude Code independently fetched a mirror of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) today and it matches Grok's version character-for-character, including 'and to ensure' and the unhyphenated forms.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)). No amendment to Element 4 identified by either AI or by Claude Code's own independent search today.
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok and Gemini substantively agree. Claude Code independently fetched the 1993 original text today and confirmed Grok's exact wording verbatim.

verifiedSources.title: Master's Responsibility and Authority
verifiedSources.variantNote: Gemini spells out 'safety management system' instead of using the 'SMS' abbreviation, and hyphenates 'shore-based'. Treated as edition/style variant, consistent with the pattern already documented for Elements 1-4.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)). Amended by resolution MSC.273(85) (adopted 4 December 2008, in force 1 July 2010): inserted 'periodically' at the start of para 5.1.5. Claude Code independently confirmed two things today: (1) a direct fetch of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) shows para 5.1.5 without 'periodically' ('reviewing the SMS...'), consistent with it being a later addition; (2) an independent web search (distinct from the sources originally supplied) confirms MSC.273(85), in force 1 July 2010, specifically added the word 'periodically' to this paragraph.
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok and Gemini independently agree on the text and on this amendment attribution. Claude Code independently corroborated both the pre-amendment 1993 wording and the specific resolution/date via separate fetch and search today.

verifiedSources.title: Resources and Personnel
verifiedSources.fullText:
6 RESOURCES AND PERSONNEL

6.1 The Company should ensure that the master is:
.1 properly qualified for command;
.2 fully conversant with the Company's SMS; and
.3 given the necessary support so that the Master's duties can be safely performed.

6.2 The Company should ensure that each ship is:
.1 manned with qualified, certificated and medically fit seafarers in accordance with national and international requirements; and
.2 appropriately manned in order to encompass all aspects of maintaining safe operations on board.

6.3 The Company should establish procedures to ensure that new personnel and personnel transferred to new assignments related to safety and protection of the environment are given proper familiarization with their duties. Instructions which are essential to be provided prior to sailing should be identified, documented and given.

6.4 The Company should ensure that all personnel involved in the Company's SMS have an adequate understanding of relevant rules, regulations, codes and guidelines.

6.5 The Company should establish and maintain procedures for identifying any training which may be required in support of the SMS and ensure that such training is provided for all personnel concerned.

6.6 The Company should establish procedures by which the ship's personnel receive relevant information on the SMS in a working language or languages understood by them.

6.7 The Company should ensure that the ship's personnel are able to communicate effectively in the execution of their duties related to the SMS.
verifiedSources.variantNote: Gemini spells out 'safety management system' instead of 'SMS' in several places; substance identical to Grok's text.
verifiedSources.amendmentHistory: Adopted 4 November 1993 (resolution A.741(18)) with a single-sentence para 6.2. Amended by resolution MSC.353(92) (adopted 21 June 2013, in force 1 January 2015): replaced para 6.2 with two sub-paragraphs adding the 'appropriately manned' requirement. Claude Code independently confirmed two things today: (1) a direct fetch of the 1993 original text (admiraltylawguide.com) shows para 6.2 as a single sentence with no sub-items and no mention of 'appropriately manned', consistent with a later amendment restructuring it; (2) an independent web search (distinct sources from those originally supplied, including imorules.com and an irclass.org technical circular) confirms MSC.353(92), adopted 21 June 2013 and in force 1 January 2015, is what actually added the 'appropriately manned' sub-paragraph.
verifiedSources.verificationMethod: Grok and Gemini agree on the substantive text of 6.2, but disagreed on which resolution amended it (Grok: MSC.353(92); Gemini: MSC.273(85)). Claude Code independently checked this today via web search and confirmed MSC.353(92) is correct, not MSC.273(85).
verifiedSources.knownDiscrepancy: Gemini attributed the 6.2 'appropriately manned' amendment to MSC.273(85) (2008/2010) instead of the correct MSC.353(92) (2013/2015). This is the third documented instance in this project of Gemini citing a specific, confident but independently-disproven MSC resolution number/date for an amendment (the first being the 1.2.2.2 attribution to MSC.104(73) instead of MSC.273(85), and the second being Gemini's 'develop' vs 'establish' error in Element 2, both documented earlier in this file). Recorded here as a pattern: Gemini's verbatim text quotes have generally been reliable, but its specific amendment/resolution-number attributions have now been wrong on two separate occasions and should not be trusted without independent primary-source cross-check, which Claude Code performed here.
